title: Medicaid Coverage of Medicare Premiums and Cost Sharing
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: If I stay eligible for Medicaid, will it pay for my Medicare premiums and cost sharing and deductibles no matter if I choose a Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan, a Medicare Advantage Plan, or regular Medicare?

accurate_complete: Stated that full Medicaid (or QMB Plus status) covers the Medicare Part B premium
Stated that Medicaid covers Medicare cost-sharing (deductibles, copays, coinsurance)
Mentioned that the level of assistance depends on the beneficiary's Medicaid eligibility category
May have mentioned the QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary) program specifically
accurate_incomplete: Mentioned premium coverage but not cost-sharing coverage (or vice versa)
Said Medicaid helps with costs but did not specify which costs
Provided partial information about coverage without the full picture
not_substantive: Said 'maybe' or 'it depends' without further explanation
incorrect: Said Medicaid does not cover Medicare premiums or cost-sharing
Said all Medicaid beneficiaries get the same level of assistance regardless of their eligibility category
Provided materially incorrect information about Medicaid coverage of Medicare costs

scoring_notes: All 3 mandatory criteria must be met for Accurate and Complete (mention of QMB is optional but strengthens the answer). The 59.5% accurate_complete baseline is relatively high for the dual-eligible scenario, suggesting this is a more tractable topic for counselors. The key nuance is that assistance level varies by Medicaid category — a blanket 'yes' without that caveat is Accurate but Incomplete.
